protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 error).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 9 stocks
   line 60:  p20.aspirate(10, source_plate[src])
   At line 60 the tip went into source_A12 (well A12 in slot 1), source_B11 (well B11 in
   slot 1), source_C4 (well C4 in slot 1), source_C7 (well C7 in slot 1) and 5 more while it
   still carried source_A12 (well A12 in slot 1), source_B3 (well B3 in slot 1), source_B11
   (well B11 in slot 1), source_C7 (well C7 in slot 1) and 5 more from an earlier step (this
   line did it 9 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next
   liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid
   drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 9 other wells: wells A2, B1,
   B2, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and 1 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A12, B11, C4, C7, D1, E5, F9, G2 and 1 more in slot 1.
   Also reached 9 other wells: wells A2, B1, B2, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and 1 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 60 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [bfcd16ef5cbc]

can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
